svg.text: 130 × 85 perfboard, 2.54 grid · viewed from ABOVE, front of vehicle LEFT · Discovery 66 × 97 plugs into P1/P2 · pin numbers UM1472 Table 5 · MEC-08 / MEC-11

Odd pins are drawn on the OUTBOARD row of each header - verify on the board before wiring. Wiring is insulated point-to-point, soldered both ends, so CROSSINGS ARE FINE - routes are drawn orthogonally for legibility, not to avoid each other.
front ◀ 130 mm ▶ rear (fascia ports) · transceiver screw terminal faces rear · GND rails join at x 105 · grid indices count 2.54 mm holes from the front-left corner
rails → P1-1 · P1-49 · P2-3 · all conn. GND · xcvr · cap −
xcvr VCC · cap + · I2C-A VCC - 100 mA ceiling
60.96 mm (25 pins), pin 1 at the CN1 end
7.3 mm outboard of the headers · 16 mm fore-aft
26.6 mm behind the Discovery - 40 × 17 module fits
P2 carries 5 V, 3 V and CAN, so the 5 V inlet, the bulk cap and the transceiver sit
on that edge. P1 carries I²C and the servo PWM, so those four connectors sit on the
opposite band. Every net reaches its pins in a short run rather than a lap of the
Every ground taps the nearer rail rather than running its own wire to a single point
- on perfboard that is the difference between a tidy board and a bird's nest. One
wire leaves at x 105 to the (−) WAGO, so the star ground of HW-06 is still a star.
PD0/PD1 reach it in under 40 mm instead of crossing the deck as flying leads, and
CAN_H/L leave as one twisted pair from the rear screw terminal - the end nearest the
Considered and rejected: its shunt carries full pack current, so merging it would
pull 12 V battery wiring onto the compute deck. It stays on plate 1 and only its I²C
It leaves P2-7, climbs the open channel at x 78 and runs along the top band to
I2C-A, tapping the transceiver on the way. Taking it from P1's VDD pins instead
would have been shorter but VDD passes through JP1 - pulling load through that
Servo rail isolation and supply limits
6V IN reaches SERVO-2 and nothing else, so the servo rail never meets a logic rail
(HW-13). As outputs both supply pins are limited to 100 mA (UM1472 §4.3) - fine for
the transceiver's ~10 mA, never for the motor module.
